messages.subject: Re: ggplot2 y not found even with stat="identity"
parts:
I think part of the problem is that you are plotting many bars on top of each other. I've modified your code for p1 to generate semitransparent bars, each with a black outline

Location_Year_MeansMg26 <- read.csv("Location_Year_Means.csv")
# Make sure Year is a factor
Location_Year_MeansMg26$Year <- factor(Location_Year_MeansMg26$Year)

ggplot(Location_Year_MeansMg26, aes(x=Location, y=logConcentration, fill=Year)) +
  geom_bar(position=position_dodge(), stat="identity", colour="black", alpha=0.1) + 
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=lwr, ymax=upr), width=.2, position=position_dodge(.9))


I'm not sure what the desired output is supposed to look like, but I'd suggest summarizing your data first, before sending to ggplot. For example, if you want 8 bars, make sure your data has 8 rows.

-Winston
